capabilities: Fetch liked videos, playlists and subscriptions via the YouTube Data API
Search, filter and sort videos by title, channel, tags and content type
Fetch YouTube captions as transcripts with timestamp links
Generate AI summaries with Gemini, OpenRouter or OpenAI and append them to notes
Create video notes and add videos to daily notes
extras: Requires a self-set-up Google Cloud project with YouTube Data API v3; in Testing mode the OAuth token expires after 7 days unless the app is published. Transcript fetching uses unofficial YouTube endpoints and may fail for some videos. Liked videos are cached locally in liked-videos.json with a .bak backup; synced devices need a plugin reload.
motivation: The author wants users to consume YouTube content more intentionally by bringing liked videos, playlists and subscriptions into Obsidian for rediscovery and note-taking.
problem: YouTube is built to keep you watching new content, not to help you revisit videos you already watched and review them with your own notes; Obsidian has no built-in way to browse your YouTube library.

relations.evidence: It is inspired by the obsidian-google-calendar plugin.
